topics.name: SAM Overview & Fundamentals
topics.description: Software asset management basics, process architecture, application overview, and recommended practices.

introduction.overview: SAM Fundamentals covers the core concepts of Software Asset Management in ServiceNow, including the SAM application features, Software Asset Workspace navigation, and publisher-specific capabilities.
introduction.whyItMatters: This domain represents 14% of the CIS-SAM exam. Questions cover SAM application functionality including Dashboards, Licensing, Discovery and Normalization, Reconciliation, Optimization, and Downgrade Rights.
introduction.keyConcepts: Understand the six main feature areas of SAM: Dashboards, Licensing, Discovery and Normalization, Reconciliation, Optimization, and Downgrade Rights. Know how to navigate the Software Asset Workspace and access key reports and analytics.
introduction.examTips: Know the navigation paths within Software Asset Workspace. Understand publisher pack add-ons and what features they enable. Results are updated with each reconciliation, not on a fixed schedule.

topics.name: Data Integrity & Sources
topics.description: Importing data, software discovery, normalization, content services, and publisher packs.

introduction.overview: Data Integrity covers how software data flows into ServiceNow, Discovery integration, normalization processes, publisher packs for specific vendors, and third-party data source integration.
introduction.whyItMatters: This domain is 28% of the exam - the second largest. Expect questions on SCCM integration, publisher packs (Adobe, Citrix, IBM, Microsoft, Oracle, SAP, VMware), discovery models, software installations, and IRE API usage.
introduction.keyConcepts: Understand the difference between software models and discovery models. Know the primary key fields for matching installations to discovery models (Publisher, Display Name, Version). Master publisher pack capabilities and when to use each.
introduction.examTips: Discovery models cannot be created manually - they're auto-created during discovery. The IRE API is used for third-party discovery integration. SCCM plugins are being deprecated in favor of Service Graph Connectors. Each publisher pack has specific license metrics.

keyConcepts: Content Library and ServiceNow Content Service

topics.name: Software Compliance Management
topics.description: Products and models, license metrics, entitlements, allocations, software reconciliation, and BYOL.

introduction.overview: Software Compliance Management covers the reconciliation process, license metrics, entitlements and allocations, compliance status calculation, and publisher-specific compliance features.
introduction.whyItMatters: This is the largest domain at 30% of the exam. Questions focus on the three tiers of reconciliation results (Product, Software Model, License Metric), IBM ILMT integration, Visual Studio licensing, and compliance calculations.
introduction.keyConcepts: Understand the three tiers of reconciliation results. Know how rights available and over-licensed amounts are calculated. Master Visual Studio subscription licensing rules including install conditions for dev/test environments.
introduction.examTips: Reconciliation runs weekly by default but can be triggered on demand. For Visual Studio, production environments require separate Microsoft licenses. License usage is based on product use, not component use for ILMT integration.

topics.name: Operational Integration
topics.description: Contract and change management, service catalog, procurement, software reclamation, and demand management.

introduction.overview: Operational Integration covers how SAM integrates with other ServiceNow processes including software reclamation workflows, demand management for application rationalization, and procurement integration.
introduction.whyItMatters: This domain represents 13% of the exam. Questions cover the reclamation workflow states, Client Software Distribution (CSD 2.0) for automated removal, demand actions, and role requirements for various operations.
introduction.keyConcepts: Understand the reclamation workflow states (Ready → Awaiting User → Awaiting Approval → Awaiting Revocation → Close Complete/Skipped). Know the five standard demand actions and the role requirements for demand creation.
introduction.examTips: CSD 2.0 automates software removal; without it, manual uninstallation is required. Demand creation requires sam_admin or sam_user PLUS it_demand_user role. PPM Standard plugin is required for demand functionality.

topics.name: Extending SAM
topics.description: Software model lifecycle, reporting, SaaS License Management, optimization, and third-party integrations.

introduction.overview: Extending SAM covers advanced capabilities including Anglepoint integration, SaaS license management, Microsoft 365 optimization, savings opportunity identification, and custom configurations.
introduction.whyItMatters: This domain represents 15% of the exam. Questions focus on Anglepoint integration (OAuth 2.0, APIs), Microsoft 365 savings identification, commit levels for enterprise subscriptions, and identifying inactive subscriptions.
introduction.keyConcepts: Understand Anglepoint integration APIs and OAuth 2.0 authentication. Know how to calculate over-licensed amounts and identify savings opportunities. Master the Last activity field for finding reclamation candidates.
introduction.examTips: Over-licensed amount = Rights available × Software entitlement unit cost. Microsoft commit levels apply to E1, E3, AND E5 subscriptions. For suite products, Last activity is the latest activity from any suite component.
